page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-64 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured with AMD EPYC 9J45 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provisions 4 physical cores supporting simultaneous multithreading, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs operating at a nominal frequency of 2.7 GHz. System memory is sized at 64.0 GB, establishing a generous memory-to-compute ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is not present on this instance, with zero GPUs allocated. The configuration does not include local disk storage, meaning persistent storage must be provisioned via network-attached block volumes. Networking features include one complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent instruction execution without contention from shared hyperthreads.

The 8:1 memory-to-core configuration delivers notable qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy services by avoiding the need to overprovision compute cores merely to acquire necessary RAM capacity. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage represents a key tradeoff, making performance dependent on network block volume throughput. This instance is suited for in-memory caching solutions, enterprise relational database deployments, ETL pipelines, and memory-intensive microservices.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-64 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio that positions it effectively for memory-centric computing. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, meaning all data persistence relies on external block volumes, and it includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. Providing a cost-effective balance for RAM-intensive tasks without requiring superfluous vCPU provisioning, this instance fits in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, moderate relational databases, ETL data transformation jobs, and backend services that benefit from dedicated execution resources.
